speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy is unlikely given the patient's age and history. The clinical picture of acute liver failure (jaundice, coagulopathy, encephalopathy) combined with a history of high-risk sexual behavior and recreational drug use strongly suggests Acute Hepatitis, likely viral (Hepatitis A, B, or C) or toxin-induced. Given the severe elevation in transaminases and bilirubin, I suspect an acute viral hepatitis or acetaminophen toxicity. I need to confirm the viral etiology immediately.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis with progression to Acute Liver Failure.
